module_title: Coastal Plains and Islands - Basic Understanding
introduction: India has a vast coastline of 7,516.6 km (including islands). The Peninsular Plateau is flanked by narrow coastal strips on the west and east. Additionally, India possesses two major island groups located in the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal.

core_concepts.title: Western Coastal Plains
core_concepts.description: Sandwiched between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea. It is a 'narrow' plain. The rivers flowing here (like Narmada, Tapi) are short and swift, so they do not form deltas; instead, they form 'Estuaries'.

core_concepts.title: Eastern Coastal Plains
core_concepts.description: Located between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal. It is much 'broader' than the western coast. Large rivers like Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Cauvery flow here and form massive, fertile 'Deltas'.

core_concepts.title: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
core_concepts.description: An elongated chain of islands located in the 'Bay of Bengal' extending from north to south. They are larger in size and more numerous and scattered. The capital is 'Port Blair'.

core_concepts.title: Lakshadweep Islands
core_concepts.description: Located in the 'Arabian Sea' close to the Malabar coast of Kerala. It is very small in area (only 32 sq km). The capital is 'Kavaratti'.

important_entities.name: 10 Degree Channel
important_entities.significance: This is one of the most frequently asked geography facts. This latitude divides the Andaman Islands (to the north) from the Nicobar Islands (to the south).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not assume both island groups formed the same way. Andaman and Nicobar are of 'Volcanic/Tectonic' origin (mountain peaks), whereas Lakshadweep islands are entirely formed of 'Coral Reefs'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: East is Broad, West is Narrow
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The massive deltas formed by the eastern rivers have pushed the land out, making the East Coast significantly broader.

exam_strategy_tips: The 'Coral' origin of Lakshadweep is a guaranteed question in basic competitive exams.
The 10 Degree Channel question is a favorite for SSC and State PCS exams. Memorize it.
